questions.questionEn: A 65-year-old male is found unresponsive in a snowbank during a blizzard. He is cold to the touch, bradycardic, and has a diminished level of consciousness. After establishing an airway and providing oxygen, which intervention is the most appropriate next step in the field?
questions.questionZh: 一名65岁男性在暴风雪中被发现倒在雪堆里，无反应。他触感冰冷，心动过缓（bradycardia），意识水平下降。在建立气道并给氧之后，现场最恰当的下一步处置是哪一项？

options.en: Rapidly rewarming the patient with hot water immersion.
options.zh: 用热水浸泡对患者进行快速复温。

options.en: Administering a sympathomimetic to increase heart rate.
options.zh: 给予拟交感神经药物（sympathomimetic）以提升心率。

options.en: Allowing the patient to exercise to generate body heat.
options.zh: 让患者活动身体以自行产热。

options.en: Removing wet clothing and applying passive insulation.
options.zh: 脱除湿衣物并进行被动保温隔热。

questions.explanationEn: BC directs providers at every licence level to remove wet and cold clothing and cover the patient with blankets or dry clothing. This patient is unresponsive with bradycardia, which points to severe hypothermia (below 28 degrees C), and for severe hypothermia BC is explicit: do not actively rewarm. Insulate to prevent further heat loss, heat the ambulance interior to 30 degrees C, and avoid rough handling. A is wrong because immersion is aggressive external rewarming that can precipitate rewarming shock and core temperature afterdrop, and it is not a field intervention. B is wrong because the bradycardia of hypothermia is an appropriate response to a depressed metabolic rate; the cold myocardium is irritable, sympathomimetics are not indicated, and this is outside PCP practice here. C is wrong because mild activity is only considered in mild to moderate hypothermia in a cooperative patient, and an unresponsive patient cannot exercise; movement itself risks precipitating a dysrhythmia.
questions.explanationZh: BC 考纲对所有执照级别的低体温处置都要求：脱除湿冷衣物，用毯子或干衣物覆盖。本例患者无反应且心动过缓，提示重度低体温（低于28 °C）；BC 对重度低体温的规定非常明确——不做主动复温，而是隔热保温防止继续散热、把救护车内加温到30 °C、避免粗暴搬动。A 错：热水浸泡属于激进的体外主动复温，可能诱发复温性休克和核心温度后降（afterdrop），也不是院前可行的操作。B 错：低体温导致的心动过缓与代谢率下降是匹配的，低温心肌易激惹，拟交感药物没有指征，此处也超出 PCP 用药授权。C 错：轻度活动只考虑用于清醒配合的轻中度低体温患者，无反应的患者无法活动，搬动本身还可能诱发心律失常。

questions.questionEn: A PCP is dispatched to a suspected chemical leak at an industrial site. The site safety officer informs the crew that the hot zone is currently inaccessible due to evolving hazards. Which action best advocates for the safety of the response team and the potential patients?
questions.questionZh: 一名 PCP 被派往某工业场地处置疑似化学品泄漏。现场安全官告知救护组：由于危害仍在演变，热区（hot zone）目前无法进入。哪项行动最能同时维护救援队伍和潜在患者的安全？

options.en: Enter the hot zone immediately to begin triage.
options.zh: 立即进入热区开始检伤分类。

options.en: Wait for the fire department to declare the scene safe.
options.zh: 在原地等待消防部门宣布现场安全。

options.en: Instruct the site safety officer to move patients to the cold zone.
options.zh: 指示现场安全官把患者转移到冷区。

options.en: Consult with the incident commander to establish a safe staging area.
options.zh: 与事故指挥官（incident commander）沟通，设立安全的待命区（staging area）。

questions.explanationEn: At a hazmat incident paramedics work inside the incident command system, and advocacy means getting a defined, safe position from which care can be delivered as soon as patients are released. Consulting the IC establishes a staging area upwind and uphill, a decontamination corridor, a communication link, and a trigger for when access becomes possible; it protects the crew and shortens the time to patient care. A converts responders into patients: an evolving hot zone requires hazmat PPE and training the PCP does not have. B is passive rather than protective; a crew that simply idles without an assigned staging position may be parked in the plume and has no plan for receiving patients. C is outside the paramedic role and dangerous, because moving contaminated patients without a decontamination plan spreads contamination to the cold zone.
questions.explanationZh: 危险物质事件中，救护人员是在事故指挥体系（ICS）内工作的，所谓倡导安全，就是争取到一个明确、安全、能在患者被移出后立即开展救治的位置。与事故指挥官沟通可以确定上风向且地势较高的待命区、洗消通道、通讯联络方式，以及何时可进入的判断依据，既保护机组，又缩短患者获得救治的时间。A 错：仍在演变的热区需要危化品级 PPE 和专门训练，贸然进入只会让救援者变成伤员。B 错：单纯等待是被动而非主动保障；没有指定待命位置的车组可能正停在烟羽路径上，也没有接收患者的预案。C 错：指挥现场安全官不属于救护员职责，且在没有洗消方案的情况下移动受污染患者，会把污染扩散到冷区。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old patient is found outdoors in 35°C heat with a history of hypertension and dementia. The patient is confused, has hot, dry skin, and a heart rate of 120 bpm. Which intervention is most appropriate for this patient's condition?
questions.questionZh: 一名78岁患者在35 °C的高温户外被发现，既往有高血压和痴呆（dementia）病史。患者意识模糊，皮肤灼热干燥，心率120次/分。针对该患者的状况，哪项处置最恰当？

options.en: Administer a nonnarcotic analgesic for suspected pain.
options.zh: 针对可疑疼痛给予非阿片类镇痛药。

options.en: Apply a warm blanket to prevent shivering.
options.zh: 盖上温热毯子以防止寒战。

options.en: Encourage the patient to walk to the ambulance.
options.zh: 鼓励患者自己走到救护车上。

options.en: Initiate active cooling measures and rapid transport.
options.zh: 启动主动降温措施并快速转运。

questions.explanationEn: Hot dry skin plus altered mental status plus tachycardia in a hot environment is heat stroke, not heat exhaustion: thermoregulation has failed and organ injury is already occurring. BC lists rapid cooling as the primary survey intervention indicated for hyperthermia, and lists heat stroke among the findings that make an adult patient unstable and therefore a transport priority. Older patients are at highest risk because antihypertensives blunt the cardiovascular response, thirst and sweating are reduced with age, and dementia removes the ability to escape the heat. A treats a problem that is not present and does nothing for core temperature. B is the opposite of what is required; the patient is not shivering and warming will worsen organ injury. C is dangerous: exertion generates further heat in an unstable patient, so bring the stretcher to the patient.
questions.explanationZh: 在高温环境中出现皮肤灼热干燥 + 意识改变 + 心动过速，属于热射病（heat stroke）而非单纯热衰竭：体温调节已经失代偿，器官损伤正在发生。BC 考纲把快速降温列为高热（hyperthermia）时的初步检查阶段干预，并把热射病列入成人不稳定患者的判定条件，因此必须同时快速转运。老年人风险最高：降压药削弱了心血管代偿，随年龄增长口渴感与排汗减少，痴呆又让患者失去主动躲避高温的能力。A 错：镇痛药既无指征，也不影响核心体温。B 错：保暖与所需处置完全相反，患者并无寒战，加温只会加重器官损伤。C 错：让不稳定患者走动会额外产热，应把担架推到患者身边。

questions.questionEn: A Paramedic is transporting a patient with complex chronic needs to a long-term care facility. The receiving nurse expresses concern that the patient's current condition may exceed the facility's capabilities. How should the Paramedic best collaborate with the nurse to ensure patient safety?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正把一位有复杂慢性照护需求的患者转送到长期照护机构。接收护士表示担忧：患者目前的状况可能超出该机构的照护能力。Paramedic 应如何与护士协作，才能最好地保障患者安全？

options.en: Instruct the nurse to contact the physician on call.
options.zh: 指示护士联系值班医生。

options.en: Request that the patient be admitted to the emergency department.
options.zh: 要求把患者改送急诊科收治。

options.en: Defer the decision to the patient's legal guardian.
options.zh: 把这个决定交给患者的法定监护人。

options.en: Discuss the patient's current clinical status and stability with the nurse.
options.zh: 与护士交流患者当前的临床状态和稳定程度。

questions.explanationEn: The nurse has raised a clinical question, and it can only be answered with clinical information: presenting problem, vital sign trend, interventions given and the response to them, and what the patient will need over the next few hours. Sharing that information turns an impasse into a joint decision, which is the core of working as part of a care team. A tells another professional what to do and hands off a decision that the paramedic still owns. B escalates to the ED before establishing whether the facility can in fact manage the patient, which risks an unnecessary emergency department visit, a lost bed and a longer time out of service. C misapplies the guardian's role: a substitute decision-maker consents to care and sets goals of care, but does not determine whether a facility is clinically capable of providing it.
questions.explanationZh: 护士提出的是一个临床问题，只有用临床信息才能回答：主诉、生命体征的变化趋势、已经给予的处置及其反应，以及未来数小时患者可能需要什么。把这些信息交流清楚，就把僵局变成了共同决策，这正是团队协作照护的核心。A 错：指挥别的专业人员做事不是协作，而且把本该自己参与的决定推了出去。B 错：在尚未弄清机构到底能不能照护之前就改送急诊，可能造成不必要的急诊就诊、床位浪费和车辆长时间脱离服务。C 错：法定监护人的角色是代为同意和确定照护目标，而不是判断某机构在临床上是否有能力照护。

questions.questionEn: While entering a residence for a medical call, a Paramedic observes heavy smoke emanating from the kitchen, several large animals loose in the hallway, and piles of newspapers blocking the exit. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
questions.questionZh: 在进入一处住宅执行医疗任务时，Paramedic 发现厨房冒出浓烟，走廊里有几只大型动物在乱窜，成堆的报纸堵住了出口。最恰当的即时处置是什么？

options.en: Assist the patient out of the house immediately.
options.zh: 立即把患者搀扶出屋。

options.en: Retreat and request fire department assistance.
options.zh: 撤离到安全处并请求消防部门支援。

options.en: Attempt to extinguish the fire with a handheld extinguisher.
options.zh: 尝试用手提灭火器灭火。

options.en: Move the animals outside to clear the path.
options.zh: 先把动物赶出屋外以清出通道。

questions.explanationEn: Three hazards are present at once: an active fire producing heavy smoke, an obstructed means of egress, and uncontrolled large animals. None of them can be managed with the equipment, PPE or training a paramedic carries, and the scene must be made safe by the agency equipped to do it before any patient contact. Withdrawing and calling fire also starts the clock on the resources that will actually solve the problem. A sends the crew and the patient through the single blocked exit into a smoke-filled structure, which is exactly how rescuers become casualties. C is firefighting in an atmosphere that may already be immediately dangerous to life and health, without SCBA and without knowing the fire's extent. D addresses the least dangerous hazard and leaves the smoke and blocked egress untouched.
questions.explanationZh: 现场同时存在三重危险：正在燃烧并产生浓烟的火源、被堵住的唯一出口、以及失控的大型动物。这三样都不是救护员携带的装备、防护和训练能够处理的，必须先由具备能力的部门把现场变安全，才能接触患者；先撤离并呼叫消防，也让真正能解决问题的资源尽早启动。A 错：让机组和患者穿过被堵塞的唯一出口进入充满烟雾的建筑，正是救援者变成伤员的典型路径。C 错：灭火作业可能发生在已达到立即危及生命与健康（IDLH）的环境中，且没有 SCBA，也不清楚火势范围。D 错：先处理了危险性最低的一项，浓烟和堵塞的出口依然存在。

questions.questionEn: According to standard precautions for infection control, which practice is required when caring for all patients regardless of their perceived or confirmed infection status?
questions.questionZh: 按照感染控制的标准预防（standard precautions）原则，在照护任何患者时——无论其感染状态是可疑还是已确诊——都必须执行的措施是哪一项？

options.en: Hand hygiene before and after patient contact.
options.zh: 在接触患者前后执行手部卫生。

options.en: Wearing a surgical mask during all patient interactions.
options.zh: 在所有患者接触过程中佩戴外科口罩。

options.en: Using sterile gloves for all primary assessments.
options.zh: 所有初步评估都使用无菌手套。

options.en: Utilizing a face shield during every patient encounter.
options.zh: 每一次接触患者都使用面屏。

questions.explanationEn: Standard precautions (routine practices) rest on the principle that infectious status is often unknown, so a baseline set of measures is applied to every patient. Hand hygiene is the element required at every single encounter and is the single most effective intervention against transmission, because hands are the final common pathway between one patient, the environment and the next patient. The other three options are risk-based additions rather than universal requirements: a surgical mask is added when droplet exposure is anticipated, a face shield when splash or spray is anticipated, and sterile gloves are reserved for sterile procedures, since clean non-sterile gloves are appropriate for routine assessment. Applying them to every encounter consumes resources without adding protection, and none of them substitutes for hand hygiene.
questions.explanationZh: 标准预防（在加拿大常称 routine practices）的前提是：患者的感染状态往往未知，因此对每一位患者都执行一套基线防护措施。其中在每一次接触中都必须执行的是手部卫生，它也是阻断传播最有效的单项措施——手是患者、环境与下一位患者之间的最终共同通路。其余三项属于按风险追加的措施而非普遍要求：预计有飞沫暴露时加戴外科口罩，预计有喷溅时加戴面屏，而无菌手套只用于无菌操作，常规评估使用清洁的非无菌手套即可。把它们用于每一次接触只会消耗资源而不增加保护，且都不能替代手部卫生。

questions.questionEn: A 45-year-old patient who is alert and oriented refuses a specific intervention. What is the primary responsibility of the paramedic in this situation?
questions.questionZh: 一名45岁、意识清醒且定向力正常的患者拒绝接受某项特定处置。此时 Paramedic 的首要职责是什么？

options.en: Explain the risks of refusing the intervention and the potential benefits of accepting it
options.zh: 向患者说明拒绝该处置的风险，以及接受它可能带来的益处

options.en: Contact the patient's next of kin to obtain consent
options.zh: 联系患者的近亲属以取得同意

options.en: Persuade the patient to accept the intervention for their own safety
options.zh: 为了患者自身安全而劝服其接受该处置

options.en: Document the refusal and immediately transport the patient to the hospital
options.zh: 记录拒绝事实，并立即把患者送往医院

questions.explanationEn: A capable adult may refuse any intervention, including a life-saving one. What the paramedic owes the patient is informed refusal, which carries the same disclosure standard as informed consent: explain what is proposed, why, the risks of declining, the benefits of accepting, and any alternatives, then confirm the patient understands and document the discussion. B is wrong because a capable patient's decision cannot be overridden by family; a substitute decision-maker only acts when the patient lacks capacity. C is wrong because persuasion shades into coercion, and pressure applied to a capable refusal invalidates the voluntariness that consent and refusal both depend on; informing and offering is legitimate, pressuring is not. D is wrong because documentation is necessary but comes after the disclosure, and transport itself requires consent, so it cannot be imposed on a patient who has refused.
questions.explanationZh: 具备决策能力的成年患者有权拒绝任何处置，包括救命性处置。救护员应尽的义务是完成知情拒绝（informed refusal），其告知标准与知情同意相同：说明拟采取的处置、理由、拒绝的风险、接受的益处以及可选替代方案，确认患者已理解，并把这段沟通记录下来。B 错：有能力患者的决定不能由家属推翻，替代决策者只有在患者丧失能力时才介入。C 错：劝服很容易滑向强迫，对一个有能力的拒绝施加压力，会破坏同意与拒绝共同依赖的自愿性；告知和提供选择是正当的，施压不是。D 错：记录确有必要，但应在充分告知之后；而且转运本身也需要同意，不能强加于已经拒绝的患者。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is transporting a term neonate who was born in a residential setting. The infant is tachypneic and exhibits mild mottling of the skin. Which action is the most appropriate to prevent further heat loss?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正在转运一名在家中出生的足月新生儿。婴儿呼吸增快（tachypnea），皮肤出现轻度花斑（mottling）。为防止进一步的热量丢失，哪项处置最恰当？

options.en: Apply a warm, damp cloth to the infant's head.
options.zh: 在婴儿头部敷上温热的湿布。

options.en: Dry the infant and wrap them in a pre-warmed blanket.
options.zh: 把婴儿擦干，并用预热过的毯子包裹。

options.en: Place the infant in a prone position on the stretcher.
options.zh: 把婴儿俯卧放在担架上。

options.en: Increase the ambient temperature of the ambulance to 30 degrees Celsius.
options.zh: 把救护车厢内的环境温度提高到30 °C。

questions.explanationEn: BC's newborn sequence begins with dry, stimulate and keep warm, and drying is what stops the dominant mechanism of neonatal heat loss. A newborn has a large surface area relative to mass, little subcutaneous fat, and cannot shiver, so evaporation from wet skin cools the infant within minutes; cold stress then drives up oxygen consumption and produces exactly the tachypnoea and mottling described. A is wrong because a damp cloth keeps the skin wet and the head is the largest single site of loss. C is wrong because position has no thermal effect and prone is not the transport position of choice. D is a legitimate adjunct, and BC does heat the ambulance for hypothermic patients, but warming the air does not stop evaporative loss from a wet infant; drying and wrapping comes first and works faster.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的新生儿处置顺序从擦干、刺激、保暖开始，而擦干正是阻断新生儿最主要散热途径的关键。新生儿体表面积相对体重大、皮下脂肪少、又不会通过寒战产热，皮肤潮湿时几分钟内就会因蒸发而失温；随之而来的冷应激会显著增加耗氧，正好表现为题干中的呼吸增快和皮肤花斑。A 错：湿布让皮肤持续潮湿，而头部恰恰是散热最多的单一部位。C 错：体位对体温没有帮助，俯卧也不是转运的首选体位。D 是合理的辅助手段（BC 对低体温患者确实要求把车厢加温），但提高环境温度并不能阻止潮湿婴儿的蒸发散热，擦干加包裹才是第一步，且见效更快。

questions.questionEn: A 6-year-old child is frightened and crying during a primary assessment following a fall. Which communication technique should the paramedic use to obtain a more accurate history from the child?
questions.questionZh: 一名6岁儿童在跌倒后接受初步评估时非常害怕、不停哭泣。Paramedic 应采用哪种沟通技巧，才能从孩子那里获得更准确的病史？

options.en: Use medical terminology to demonstrate professional authority.
options.zh: 使用医学术语以显示专业权威。

options.en: Ask the child's parent to answer all questions for the child.
options.zh: 让孩子的家长代替孩子回答全部问题。

options.en: Get down to the child's eye level and use simple language.
options.zh: 蹲下与孩子平视，并使用简单的语言。

options.en: Instruct the child to be quiet so the assessment can be completed.
options.zh: 要求孩子安静下来，以便完成评估。

questions.explanationEn: A frightened child gives poor information, and fear also inflates the physical findings by driving heart rate and respiratory rate. Coming down to eye level removes the looming adult in uniform, and short concrete words matched to a 6-year-old's vocabulary let the child answer questions that only the child can answer, such as where it hurts and what happened. A is wrong because unfamiliar terminology increases fear and produces no usable answers. B is wrong because a parent supplies valuable context but cannot report the child's symptoms; school-age children localize pain reliably and are the primary source for the mechanism they experienced. D is wrong because demanding silence removes the history altogether and increases distress, which further distorts the vital signs.
questions.explanationZh: 受惊吓的孩子提供的信息质量很差，而且恐惧本身会拉高心率和呼吸频率，干扰体征判断。蹲下与孩子平视，去掉了那个居高临下、穿着制服的成人形象；用符合6岁孩子词汇量的简短具体的说法提问，才能得到只有孩子本人能回答的信息——哪里疼、当时发生了什么。A 错：陌生的医学术语只会加重恐惧，得不到可用的回答。B 错：家长能提供重要的背景信息，但无法替孩子描述症状；学龄儿童对疼痛部位的定位相当可靠，也是事发经过的第一手来源。D 错：要求孩子安静等于放弃了病史采集，还会加重痛苦，进一步扭曲生命体征。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old patient has partial-thickness burns to the entire right arm and the anterior chest only, with the abdomen spared. Using the adult Rule of Nines, what TBSA is burned?
questions.questionZh: 一名82岁患者的整个右上肢以及前胸（腹部未受累）为部分厚度烧伤（partial-thickness burn）。按成人九分法（Rule of Nines）计算，烧伤的体表总面积（TBSA）是多少？
questions.explanationEn: In the adult Rule of Nines each entire upper limb is 9 percent (4.5 percent anterior plus 4.5 percent posterior), and the anterior trunk is 18 percent, conventionally divided into 9 percent anterior chest and 9 percent anterior abdomen. Whole right arm 9 plus anterior chest 9 equals 18 percent. A (13.5) comes from counting only the anterior half of the arm; B (14.5) has no anatomical basis; D (22.5) adds the anterior abdomen, which the stem explicitly spares, or double counts part of the arm. The number is not academic: BC requires BSA to be calculated during the primary survey, partial thickness burns over 20 percent BSA make an adult patient unstable, and burns over 20 percent BSA are an indication for the PCP hypovolemia and fluid protocol.
questions.explanationZh: 成人九分法中，每一条完整上肢为 9%（前面 4.5% + 后面 4.5%），躯干前面共 18%，习惯上分为前胸 9% 与前腹 9%。整个右上肢 9% + 前胸 9% = 18%。A（13.5%）是只算了上肢的前半面；B（14.5%）没有任何解剖学依据；D（22.5%）要么把题干明确排除的前腹算了进去，要么重复计算了上肢的一部分。这个数字并非纸上谈兵：BC 要求在初步检查阶段计算体表面积，部分厚度烧伤超过 20% BSA 即判定成人患者为不稳定，而超过 20% BSA 的烧伤也是 PCP 低血容量与补液流程的启动指征。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is preparing to enter a scene where a patient is suspected of having a highly contagious respiratory infection. Which piece of personal protective equipment (PPE) provides the most appropriate level of protection for this specific risk?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 准备进入一个现场，该处患者被怀疑患有高传染性呼吸道感染。针对这一特定风险，哪一件个人防护装备（PPE）提供的防护级别最恰当？

options.en: Sterile surgical gloves.
options.zh: 无菌外科手套。

options.en: An N95 respirator.
options.zh: N95 呼吸防护口罩。

options.en: A face shield.
options.zh: 面屏。

options.en: A fluid-resistant gown.
options.zh: 防液体渗透的隔离衣。

questions.explanationEn: The hazard named in the stem is inhalation of infectious aerosols, so the PPE that addresses it must filter what the provider breathes. An N95 respirator filters at least 95 percent of airborne particles and, unlike a surgical mask, is designed to seal to the face, which is why fit testing and a seal check each time are required. Gloves interrupt contact transmission, a face shield protects the mucous membranes of the eyes from splash and spray but leaves the airway unprotected, and a gown protects skin and clothing. All three are appropriate parts of a full ensemble alongside the respirator, but none of them addresses the specific respiratory route the question asks about, and sterile gloves in particular offer no advantage over clean gloves here.
questions.explanationZh: 题干指明的危险是吸入含病原体的气溶胶，因此对应的防护必须过滤救护员吸入的空气。N95 呼吸器可过滤至少 95% 的空气传播微粒，且与外科口罩不同，它的设计目标是与面部形成密合，这也是为什么必须做适合性检验（fit test）并在每次佩戴时做密合性检查。手套阻断的是接触传播；面屏保护眼部黏膜免受喷溅，但对呼吸道毫无防护；隔离衣保护皮肤和衣物。这三者与呼吸器一起构成完整的防护组合都是合理的，但都无法解决题目所问的呼吸道传播途径；本例中无菌手套相比清洁手套也没有任何额外好处。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic arrives at a scene where a chemical spill has occurred in an industrial park. After donning appropriate personal protective equipment, the paramedic observes several victims with varying degrees of respiratory distress and skin irritation. Which action is the priority during the initial triage of these patients?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 抵达某工业园区的化学品泄漏现场。在穿戴好合适的个人防护装备后，他观察到多名伤者出现不同程度的呼吸窘迫和皮肤刺激。对这些患者进行初期检伤分类时，哪项应优先？

options.en: Decontaminate patients before initiating further clinical assessment.
options.zh: 在开始进一步临床评估之前，先对患者进行洗消（decontamination）。

options.en: Perform a full primary survey on the most critically injured patient.
options.zh: 对伤势最重的患者完成完整的初步检查。

options.en: Administer a sympathomimetic bronchodilator to patients with wheezing.
options.zh: 给出现喘鸣的患者使用拟交感支气管扩张剂。

options.en: Transport the first available patient to the nearest hospital.
options.zh: 把第一个能搬走的患者送往最近的医院。

questions.explanationEn: In a chemical incident decontamination precedes definitive assessment and treatment for two reasons: as long as the agent remains on the patient it continues to be absorbed and off-gassed, so removing clothing and the agent is itself the first and most effective treatment; and an undecontaminated patient contaminates responders, the ambulance and the receiving emergency department, which can force the department to close. B is wrong because a hands-on primary survey on a contaminated patient exposes the provider and delays removal of the agent, which is the intervention that actually changes the patient's trajectory. C is wrong because a bronchodilator does not stop ongoing exposure, and drug administration is not performed in the warm zone. D is wrong because transporting a contaminated patient spreads the agent along the entire care pathway.
questions.explanationZh: 化学事件中，洗消要先于确定性的评估与处置，原因有两点：只要毒物还留在患者身上，它就会持续被吸收并向外挥发，因此脱除衣物、清除毒物本身就是第一位且最有效的治疗；同时，未经洗消的患者会污染救援人员、救护车和接收医院的急诊科，甚至可能迫使急诊科关闭。B 错：对受污染患者做接触式的初步检查，不仅让施救者暴露，还推迟了真正能改变病情走向的处置（清除毒物）。C 错：支气管扩张剂无法阻止持续的暴露，而且在温区不进行给药操作。D 错：转运未洗消的患者会把污染沿整条救治链扩散。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is operating an ambulance on a rural highway during a severe winter storm with limited visibility and black ice. The partner is in the back with a stable patient. Which action best ensures the safety of the crew and patient during transport?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 在严冬暴风雪中于乡村公路上驾驶救护车，能见度很低且路面有黑冰（black ice）。搭档在车厢后部照护一名病情稳定的患者。哪项做法最能保障机组与患者在转运途中的安全？

options.en: Increase the speed to reach the destination hospital more quickly.
options.zh: 提高车速以尽快抵达目的地医院。

options.en: Reduce speed and increase the following distance from the vehicle ahead.
options.zh: 降低车速并加大与前车的跟车距离。

options.en: Turn off the emergency lights to improve the visibility of other drivers.
options.zh: 关闭警灯以改善其他驾驶者的视野。

options.en: Instruct the partner to move to the front seat for better stability.
options.zh: 让搭档移到前排座位以获得更好的稳定性。

questions.explanationEn: On black ice available traction collapses, and stopping distance can be several times what it is on dry pavement; a heavy, high-centre-of-gravity ambulance is particularly unforgiving. Reducing speed and extending the following distance are the two variables the driver actually controls, and they address both loss of control and rear-end collision. A is wrong because speed is the dominant factor in both stopping distance and loss of control, and the patient is stable, so nothing about the clinical situation justifies the added risk. C is wrong because emergency lighting makes the ambulance conspicuous in poor visibility, which is exactly when it is most needed. D is wrong because the patient cannot be left unattended in the back, and every occupant must remain properly restrained in a designated seating position.
questions.explanationZh: 黑冰路面上可用的附着力大幅下降，制动距离可能是干燥路面的数倍；救护车重量大、重心高，容错空间尤其小。降低车速与加大跟车距离，是驾驶员真正能控制的两个变量，同时应对失控和追尾两种风险。A 错：车速是决定制动距离和失控概率的首要因素，而患者病情稳定，临床上并无任何理由承担这份额外风险。C 错：能见度差的时候恰恰最需要警灯来提高本车的可见性。D 错：患者不能被独自留在车厢后部，且所有乘员都必须在指定座位上系好约束装置。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is called to a home where an adult patient is experiencing a medical emergency. The patient's family members are present and express that their traditional healing practices must be integrated into the care plan. The patient is currently unable to communicate. Which approach best demonstrates cultural safety and equity in this situation?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 出诊到某住宅，一位成年患者正处于医疗急症中。家属在场，并表示必须把他们的传统疗愈习俗纳入照护方案。患者目前无法进行沟通。哪种做法最能体现文化安全（cultural safety）与公平？

options.en: Explain that traditional practices must wait until the patient is at the hospital.
options.zh: 说明传统习俗必须等患者送到医院之后再进行。

options.en: Inform the family that evidence-based medicine takes precedence over tradition.
options.zh: 告知家属循证医学优先于传统习俗。

options.en: Ask the family how their traditional practices can be safely incorporated into the care.
options.zh: 询问家属，他们的传统习俗可以如何安全地融入到照护当中。

options.en: Request that the family leave the room to allow the paramedic to work efficiently.
options.zh: 请家属离开房间，以便自己高效工作。

questions.explanationEn: Cultural safety is judged by the patient and family, not by the provider, and the practical question is almost never whether to allow a practice but how to accommodate it without compromising care. Asking opens that negotiation and usually reveals that the practice is entirely compatible with emergency care: prayer, the presence of an elder, a medicine bundle kept with the patient, smudging performed outside the vehicle. It also protects access, because a family who feels dismissed may withhold history or decline transport. A and B are provider-centred refusals that create the very barrier this competency asks paramedics to remove, and B frames the situation as a contest that no one needs to win. D removes the only people who can speak for a patient unable to communicate, discarding both the history and the substitute decision-maker.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全的评判者是患者和家属，而不是医疗提供者；现实中的问题几乎从来不是要不要允许某项习俗，而是如何在不影响救治的前提下安排它。主动询问打开了协商空间，而结果往往是：这些习俗与急救完全可以并存——祈祷、由长者陪同、随身携带药囊、在车外完成熏香仪式等。这样做同时也保护了医疗可及性，因为感到被轻视的家属可能不再提供病史，甚至拒绝转运。A、B 都是以提供者为中心的拒绝，恰恰制造了这项胜任力要求救护员去消除的障碍；B 更把情境框成了一场无谓的输赢之争。D 错：把唯一能替无法沟通的患者发声的人赶走，等于同时丢掉了病史来源和替代决策者。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic has been working a series of mandatory overtime shifts due to staffing shortages and is beginning to experience difficulty concentrating during patient handovers. Which strategy is the most effective way for the paramedic to manage their fitness to practise in this situation?
questions.questionZh: 由于人手短缺，一名 Paramedic 连续上了多个强制加班班次，如今在做患者交接时开始出现注意力难以集中的情况。要管理自己的执业适任状态（fitness to practise），哪种策略最有效？

options.en: Increasing caffeine intake to maintain alertness during the shift.
options.zh: 增加咖啡因摄入，以维持当班时的警觉度。

options.en: Communicating the fatigue to the partner and supervisor to adjust tasks.
options.zh: 把疲劳状况告知搭档和主管，以便调整任务分配。

options.en: Requesting a transfer to a lower-volume station for the remainder of the week.
options.zh: 申请本周余下时间调到出车量较小的站点。

options.en: Utilizing a stimulant medication to counteract the effects of sleep deprivation.
options.zh: 使用兴奋类药物来对抗睡眠剥夺的影响。

questions.explanationEn: Fatigue that is already degrading concentration during handover is a present patient-safety hazard, not a future one, because handover is where medication doses, allergies and time-critical findings are transferred. Disclosing it and redistributing tasks is the only option that reduces risk during the shift in progress: the partner can lead the handover, drug calculations can be double-checked, driving can be reassigned, and the supervisor gains the information needed to fix the roster. It is also the accountable act, since fitness to practise is a self-monitoring obligation. A masks a symptom, does nothing for judgement or vigilance decrement, and worsens the sleep that follows. C is a scheduling remedy for later in the week and leaves today's calls unprotected. D is unsafe self-medication and is not a professional response to sleep debt.
questions.explanationZh: 已经影响到交接时注意力的疲劳，是当下而非将来的患者安全风险——交接恰恰是传递用药剂量、过敏史和时间关键性发现的环节。主动说出疲劳并重新分配任务，是四个选项中唯一能在本班次内立即降低风险的做法：可以让搭档主导交接、对药物计算做双人复核、把驾驶任务转交，主管也才拿到调整排班所需的信息。这同时是负责任的行为，因为执业适任本身就是一项自我监测义务。A 只是掩盖症状，对判断力下降和警觉度衰减无济于事，还会破坏随后的睡眠。C 是针对本周稍后时段的排班补救，今天的出车依然没有保护。D 属于不安全的自行用药，不是应对睡眠负债的专业做法。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is treating a patient whose primary language is not English and who has limited health literacy. The patient's family is present and attempting to translate the paramedic's questions. Which communication approach is most appropriate to ensure the patient's needs are understood and met?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正在照护一位母语非英语、健康素养有限的患者。患者家属在场，并试图为 Paramedic 的提问做翻译。为确保准确理解并满足患者的需求，哪种沟通方式最恰当？

options.en: Speaking louder and slower to the patient to improve comprehension.
options.zh: 对患者更大声、更慢地讲话，以帮助其理解。

options.en: Asking the family members to summarize the patient's medical history.
options.zh: 请家属概括叙述患者的病史。

options.en: Using a certified medical translation service to facilitate communication.
options.zh: 使用有资质的医疗翻译服务来完成沟通。

options.en: Writing down instructions for the patient to read after the call.
options.zh: 把指示写下来，让患者事后阅读。

questions.explanationEn: A trained medical interpreter renders what is said accurately and completely, is bound by confidentiality, and has no stake in the outcome. Family interpreters routinely omit, soften or edit, particularly around substance use, sexual and reproductive history, intimate partner violence and prognosis; they may answer on the patient's behalf, and children should never be used. Because interpretation errors change the history, they change the working diagnosis. A confuses a language barrier with a hearing barrier and is experienced as condescending. B abandons the patient's own account for a second-hand summary and compounds the same filtering problem. D fails a patient with limited health literacy, is likely in the wrong language, and provides nothing at the moment the information is actually needed.
questions.explanationZh: 受过训练的医疗翻译能够准确、完整地传达双方所说的内容，负有保密义务，且对结果没有利害关系。由家属充当翻译时，遗漏、软化和自行删改是常态，尤其涉及物质使用、性与生殖史、亲密伴侣暴力和预后等话题；家属还常常越俎代庖替患者作答，而未成年人绝不应担任翻译。由于翻译差错会改变病史，也就直接改变了初步判断。A 把语言障碍误当成听力障碍，患者通常会感到被轻视。B 用二手概述取代了患者本人的陈述，同样存在信息过滤问题。D 对健康素养有限的患者无效，语言很可能仍不匹配，而且在真正需要信息的当下什么也没解决。

questions.questionEn: While responding to a multi-vehicle collision, you observe a placard on a leaking tanker truck indicating a hazardous material. The wind is blowing directly toward your ambulance and the nearby crowd. What is the most appropriate action to take to ensure the safety of yourself and the public?
questions.questionZh: 在处置一起多车相撞事故时，你注意到一辆正在泄漏的罐车上贴有危险品标示牌（placard）。风正朝着你的救护车和附近人群的方向吹。为保障自身与公众的安全，最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Park the ambulance upwind and uphill from the scene.
options.zh: 把救护车停在现场的上风向且地势较高处。

options.en: Approach the tanker to identify the specific chemical.
options.zh: 靠近罐车以辨认具体的化学物质。

options.en: Instruct bystanders to evacuate in the direction of the wind.
options.zh: 指挥旁观者顺着风向撤离。

options.en: Begin triage of patients closest to the leak.
options.zh: 先对最靠近泄漏点的伤者进行检伤分类。

questions.explanationEn: Upwind and uphill is the standing rule for hazardous material positioning, because many vapours are heavier than air and travel downwind and downhill, and liquid runoff follows the same path. Positioning this way also preserves an escape route and keeps the vehicle usable rather than contaminated. B defeats the purpose of isolation distances: the placard number can be read at distance with binoculars and looked up in the Emergency Response Guidebook, which is exactly why placards exist. C is the most dangerous instruction in the set, since evacuating downwind moves the public through the plume. D places the crew inside the hot zone; patients closest to the leak must be moved out and decontaminated by trained hazmat responders before paramedic contact, or the crew simply becomes the next set of patients.
questions.explanationZh: 上风向、地势高，是危险物质现场停车定位的通用铁律：许多蒸气比空气重，会顺风且向低处流动，泄漏的液体同样往低处走。这样停车还保留了撤离路线，并使车辆保持可用而不被污染。B 错：这正好抵消了隔离距离的意义——标示牌上的编号可以在远处用望远镜读取，再查《应急响应指南》（ERG），标示牌的存在就是为了让人不必靠近。C 是四个选项中最危险的指令：顺风撤离等于把人群赶进烟羽。D 错：这会把机组置于热区之内；最靠近泄漏点的伤者必须由受过训练的危化品救援人员移出并完成洗消，救护员才能接触，否则机组就是下一批伤员。

questions.questionEn: You are treating a 75-year-old patient found outdoors in winter. The patient is shivering, alert, and oriented, but complaining of numbness in their fingers and toes. Which finding would most accurately indicate that the patient's condition is deteriorating from mild to moderate hypothermia?
questions.questionZh: 你正在处置一名75岁患者，他在冬季户外被发现。患者目前发抖、清醒、定向力正常，但主诉手指和脚趾麻木。哪一项发现最能准确提示患者正从轻度低体温恶化为中度低体温？

options.en: The patient begins to complain of extreme fatigue.
options.zh: 患者开始主诉极度疲乏。

options.en: The patient's skin becomes pale and cool to the touch.
options.zh: 患者皮肤变得苍白、触感发凉。

options.en: The patient reports a loss of dexterity in their hands.
options.zh: 患者诉说双手灵巧度下降。

options.en: The patient stops shivering and becomes lethargic.
options.zh: 患者停止发抖，并变得昏沉嗜睡。

questions.explanationEn: Shivering is the body's main endogenous heat production mechanism, and it fails as the core temperature falls toward the low 30s. Cessation of shivering together with a falling level of consciousness is the classic marker that a patient has crossed from mild into moderate hypothermia. BC defines mild as above 32 and below 35 degrees C and moderate as above 28 to below 32 degrees C; both are managed with active rewarming, while severe hypothermia below 28 degrees C must not be actively rewarmed, so recognizing where the patient sits changes what you actually do. A, B and C are all findings of mild hypothermia in a patient who is still compensating: fatigue, peripheral vasoconstriction producing pale cool skin, and loss of fine motor dexterity appear early and do not by themselves signal deterioration.
questions.explanationZh: 寒战（发抖）是人体最主要的内源性产热方式，当核心体温降到 32 °C 上下时它会衰竭。寒战停止并伴随意识水平下降，是患者由轻度跨入中度低体温的经典标志。BC 把轻度定义为 >32 °C 且 <35 °C，中度为 >28 °C 至 <32 °C，两者都需要主动复温；而低于 28 °C 的重度低体温则禁止主动复温——所以判断患者处于哪一档，直接决定你的处置。A、B、C 都属于仍在代偿阶段的轻度低体温表现：疲乏、外周血管收缩导致皮肤苍白发凉、精细动作灵巧度下降，都出现得较早，单凭它们并不能说明病情正在恶化。

questions.questionEn: You are caring for an elderly patient with advanced dementia who is being transported to a long-term care facility. The patient has an active cough and is sneezing frequently. Which action best balances infection control with the need for patient comfort and dignity?
questions.questionZh: 你正在照护一位患有晚期痴呆的老年患者，正把他转运到长期照护机构。患者有活动性咳嗽并频繁打喷嚏。哪项做法最能在感染控制与患者舒适和尊严之间取得平衡？

options.en: Require the patient to wear a mask for the duration of the trip.
options.zh: 要求患者在全程佩戴口罩。

options.en: Implement droplet precautions and perform hand hygiene.
options.zh: 实施飞沫预防措施并执行手部卫生。

options.en: Isolate the patient in the rear of the ambulance away from the crew.
options.zh: 把患者隔离在救护车后部，远离机组人员。

options.en: Avoid all physical contact with the patient during transport.
options.zh: 在整个转运过程中避免与患者的一切身体接触。

questions.explanationEn: Droplet precautions address the actual route of transmission while leaving the patient's care untouched: the provider wears a mask and eye protection, hand hygiene is performed before and after contact, source control is offered to the patient as tolerated, ventilation in the compartment is increased, and the compartment is cleaned afterwards. A is a reasonable adjunct but not the answer as written, because a patient with advanced dementia may not tolerate a mask and enforcing one for an entire trip risks agitation, airway compromise and functions as a restraint. C is not achievable: the attendant must stay with the patient in the patient compartment, and distance alone in a small closed space is not a precaution. D is unsafe, since assessment, reassessment and reassurance all require contact, and avoiding touch does not prevent droplet spread.
questions.explanationZh: 飞沫预防措施针对的正是实际的传播途径，同时完全不影响对患者的照护：救护员佩戴口罩和眼部防护，接触前后执行手部卫生，在患者可耐受的前提下为其提供源头控制（口罩），加强车厢通风，转运后清洁消毒。A 是合理的辅助手段但不是本题答案：晚期痴呆患者可能无法耐受口罩，强制全程佩戴会引发躁动、危及气道，实质上等同于一种约束。C 不可行：随车照护者必须留在车厢内陪伴患者，在狭小密闭空间里仅靠拉开距离并不构成防护措施。D 不安全：评估、复评和安抚都需要接触，而且避免触碰并不能阻止飞沫传播。

questions.questionEn: A Paramedic is asked to provide a formal statement regarding a patient's medical history to a third-party insurance company without the patient's explicit written consent. Which action best fulfills the Paramedic's legal and ethical obligations?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 被要求在未取得患者明确书面同意的情况下，向第三方保险公司提供关于该患者病史的正式陈述。哪项做法最符合 Paramedic 的法律与伦理义务？

options.en: Provide the requested information immediately to ensure the patient's claim is processed.
options.zh: 立即提供所需信息，以确保患者的理赔能够顺利处理。

options.en: Verify that the patient has provided authorization for the release of their health information.
options.zh: 先核实患者是否已授权披露其健康信息。

options.en: Consult with the patient's primary care physician to obtain the necessary records.
options.zh: 联系患者的家庭医生以取得所需记录。

options.en: Inform the insurance company that the information is available upon request from the hospital.
options.zh: 告知保险公司可以向医院索取该信息。

questions.explanationEn: Personal health information may be disclosed only with the patient's consent or under a specific legal authority such as a subpoena or a statutory reporting duty. Helping a claim proceed is not a legal authority, and the requester's convenience does not create one. Verifying that a valid, current authorization exists, and that it covers this information and this requester, is the step that satisfies both the legislation and the professional obligation to adhere to regulatory requirements. A is a privacy breach regardless of good intent. C compounds the breach by gathering still more information for a purpose the patient has not authorized. D deflects rather than protects: it implies the disclosure is acceptable as long as someone else makes it, and it already confirms to the insurer that records exist and where.
questions.explanationZh: 个人健康信息只能在取得患者同意、或依据传票、法定报告义务等特定法律授权的情况下披露。帮助理赔顺利进行并不构成法律授权，请求方的便利更不构成授权。核实是否存在有效且在有效期内的授权，并确认该授权覆盖这次的信息范围与请求方，才是既满足隐私立法、又满足遵守监管要求这一职业义务的做法。A 无论出发点多好，都是隐私泄露。C 更进一步：为患者未授权的目的去搜集更多信息，等于扩大了泄露。D 只是回避而非保护：它暗示只要换个人来披露就没问题，而且已经向保险公司确认了记录的存在和所在位置。

questions.questionEn: During a large-scale industrial chemical leak, a Paramedic identifies that several displaced residents from a low-income housing complex lack access to transportation to reach the designated community decontamination site. Which action best addresses this population health barrier?
questions.questionZh: 在一起大规模工业化学品泄漏事件中，一名 Paramedic 发现：来自某低收入住宅区的多名被疏散居民没有交通工具，无法抵达指定的社区洗消点。哪项行动最能解决这一人群健康层面的障碍？

options.en: Advise the residents to wait for the chemical plume to dissipate.
options.zh: 建议居民等待化学烟羽自行消散。

options.en: Instruct the residents to seek shelter in place until further notice.
options.zh: 指示居民就地避难，等待进一步通知。

options.en: Direct the residents to the nearest commercial taxi stand.
options.zh: 指引居民前往最近的商业出租车候客点。

options.en: Coordinate with the incident commander to arrange shuttle transport.
options.zh: 与事故指挥官协调，安排接驳车辆运送居民。

questions.explanationEn: The barrier here is structural rather than clinical: these residents need decontamination and cannot reach it because they have no vehicle and no money for one. Advocacy at the system level means using the incident command structure to obtain the resource that removes the barrier, in this case buses or shuttle vehicles, which is exactly the kind of population-level response an incident commander can authorize. A leaves contaminated people contaminated and exposed while the agent continues to be absorbed. B contradicts the situation: they have already been displaced from their homes and still require decontamination, so sheltering in place neither protects them nor decontaminates them. C ignores both the cost barrier that defines the problem and the fact that an unwitting taxi driver and vehicle would be contaminated in the process.
questions.explanationZh: 这里的障碍是结构性的而非临床的：这些居民需要洗消，却因为没有车、也负担不起车费而到不了洗消点。系统层面的倡导，意味着借助事故指挥体系去争取能消除障碍的资源——本例中就是巴士或接驳车辆，而这恰恰是事故指挥官有权调度的人群层面响应。A 错：让受污染的人继续留在污染中，毒物仍在持续被吸收。B 与情境矛盾：他们已经被疏散离家，且仍需洗消，就地避难既不能保护他们也不能去除污染。C 错：既无视了构成本题核心问题的经济障碍，也忽略了在毫不知情的情况下让出租车司机和车辆一并受到污染的后果。

questions.questionEn: A 12-year-old patient requires a sympathomimetic bronchodilator for acute asthma. The patient is anxious and hesitant, but the parent has provided consent. How should the Paramedic best proceed to ensure the patient's cooperation and understanding?
questions.questionZh: 一名12岁患者因急性哮喘发作需要使用拟交感支气管扩张剂。患儿感到焦虑、犹豫，但家长已给予同意。Paramedic 应如何处理，才能最好地取得患儿的配合与理解？

options.en: Administer the medication quickly to prevent further respiratory decline.
options.zh: 迅速给药，以防呼吸状况进一步恶化。

options.en: Tell the patient that the medication is mandatory for their recovery.
options.zh: 告诉患儿这个药是必须用的，为了让他康复。

options.en: Ask the parent to explain the benefits of the medication to the child.
options.zh: 请家长向孩子解释这个药的好处。

options.en: Explain the purpose of the medication in age-appropriate language.
options.zh: 用符合其年龄的语言，向患儿解释用药的目的。

questions.explanationEn: Legal consent here comes from the parent, but assent from the child determines whether a nebulizer mask is actually tolerated, and a struggling child receives far less drug than a cooperative one. Obtaining and documenting informed consent by explaining the rationale, risks and benefits whenever feasible applies to the patient in front of you, in terms that patient can use: this medicine opens the small tubes in your lungs so breathing gets easier, it tastes odd and may make your heart feel fast and your hands shaky for a while. A skips the patient entirely and, with a mask held against a resisting face, usually delivers a poor dose. B is coercive and inaccurate as phrased, and it teaches the child that clinicians do not explain. C outsources to the parent the clinician's own duty to explain the treatment being given.
questions.explanationZh: 本例中法律意义上的同意来自家长，但真正决定雾化面罩能否被接受的是患儿本人的赞同（assent）——挣扎抗拒的孩子实际吸入的药量远少于配合的孩子。在可行的情况下，通过说明理由、风险与益处来取得并记录知情同意，这项义务是针对眼前这位患者的，而且要用他能听懂的说法：这个药会把你肺里的小管子撑开，让呼吸变轻松；味道有点怪，可能会让你觉得心跳快、手有点抖，过一会儿就好。A 完全跳过了患者，而把面罩按在抗拒的脸上通常只能给到很差的剂量。B 既有强迫性，措辞也不准确，还会让孩子学到医护人员是不解释的。C 把临床人员自己解释所给治疗的义务外包给了家长。

questions.questionEn: During the initial steps of neonatal resuscitation, a newborn remains apneic and bradycardic despite drying, warming, and stimulation. What is the most appropriate next intervention?
questions.questionZh: 在新生儿复苏的初始步骤中，一名新生儿在擦干、保暖和刺激之后仍然没有呼吸（apnea）且心率过缓。最恰当的下一步处置是什么？

options.en: Initiate positive pressure ventilation.
options.zh: 开始正压通气（PPV）。

options.en: Perform chest compressions.
options.zh: 开始胸外按压。

options.en: Administer a sympathomimetic.
options.zh: 给予拟交感神经药物。

options.en: Insert an oropharyngeal airway.
options.zh: 置入口咽通气道。

questions.explanationEn: BC's newborn sequence is stepwise and driven by heart rate. Step 1 is dry, stimulate and keep warm for 30 seconds; if the heart rate is still below 100 bpm, step 2 is to ventilate with a BVM on room air for 30 seconds; if it remains below 100, step 3 adds 100 percent oxygen for 30 seconds; only if the heart rate is still below 100 after that does step 4 add chest compressions with ventilations until the heart rate is above 60. Ventilation is the intervention that resuscitates almost every newborn, because neonatal bradycardia is hypoxic in origin rather than cardiac. B is premature and is reached only after adequate ventilation has failed. C is not the PCP answer and does not correct the underlying hypoxia. D is not part of the initial steps; the newborn airway is opened by positioning in a neutral or slightly extended sniffing position and by suctioning only if secretions obstruct.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的新生儿处置流程是逐级推进、以心率为驱动的。第一步：擦干、刺激、保暖 30 秒；若心率仍 <100 次/分，第二步：用球囊面罩以室内空气通气 30 秒；仍 <100，第三步：接 100% 氧气通气 30 秒；只有在此之后心率仍 <100，第四步才加上胸外按压配合通气，直至心率升到 60 次/分以上。通气几乎能复苏所有出生后转换失败的新生儿，因为新生儿的心动过缓源于缺氧而非心脏本身的问题。B 过早：只有在充分通气仍无效之后才轮到按压。C 不是 PCP 的答案，也无法纠正根本的缺氧。D 不属于初始步骤：新生儿气道靠中立位或轻度后仰的嗅物位来开放，只有在分泌物造成阻塞时才吸引。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with increased shortness of breath and a productive cough. Which clinical finding most strongly suggests the development of acute pneumonia rather than a COPD exacerbation?
questions.questionZh: 一名78岁、有慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）病史的患者出现气促加重和咳痰。哪一项临床发现最能提示患者发生的是急性肺炎，而不是单纯的 COPD 急性加重？

options.en: Presence of wheezing on auscultation.
options.zh: 听诊闻及哮鸣音。

options.en: Increased use of accessory muscles.
options.zh: 辅助呼吸肌的使用增加。

options.en: A history of tobacco use.
options.zh: 有吸烟史。

options.en: New onset of fever and localized crackles.
options.zh: 新出现发热，并伴有局限性湿啰音。

questions.explanationEn: Pneumonia is an infection producing consolidation in a defined area of lung, so the findings that distinguish it are systemic infection plus a focal auscultatory abnormality: new fever with crackles confined to one region. A and B do not discriminate, because wheeze and accessory muscle use are expected in any COPD exacerbation and reflect airflow obstruction and increased work of breathing regardless of cause. C explains why the patient has COPD at all but says nothing about today's problem. In practice the two frequently coexist, since infection is a common trigger of an exacerbation, and BC manages both with a position of comfort, oxygen titrated to saturation and salbutamol; the distinction matters mainly for recognizing sepsis risk and for what the receiving hospital is told.
questions.explanationZh: 肺炎是感染在肺内某一区域造成实变，因此把它区分出来的表现是全身性感染 + 局灶性听诊异常：新出现的发热，加上局限于某一区域的湿啰音。A 与 B 没有鉴别力：哮鸣音和辅助呼吸肌使用在任何一次 COPD 急性加重中都可以出现，它们反映的是气流受限和呼吸做功增加，与病因无关。C 解释的是患者为什么会得 COPD，而不是今天发生了什么。实际工作中两者常常并存——感染本身就是急性加重的常见诱因；BC 对二者的院前处置也一致：舒适体位、按血氧滴定给氧、给予沙丁胺醇。做这个区分的意义主要在于识别脓毒症风险，以及在交接时向接收医院说清楚。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic experiences recurring sleep disturbances and intrusive thoughts following a series of high-acuity cardiac arrest calls. Which approach best supports their long-term psychological resilience?
questions.questionZh: 在连续处置多起高危重症心搏骤停出车之后，一名 Paramedic 反复出现睡眠障碍和侵入性回忆（intrusive thoughts）。哪种做法最有利于其长期的心理韧性？

options.en: Avoiding discussion of the calls to prevent emotional rumination.
options.zh: 避免谈论这些出车经历，以免反复咀嚼情绪。

options.en: Increasing caffeine intake to maintain alertness during shifts.
options.zh: 增加咖啡因摄入，以维持当班时的警觉度。

options.en: Utilizing peer support systems and professional mental health resources.
options.zh: 利用同僚支持体系和专业心理健康资源。

options.en: Requesting a permanent transfer to a lower-volume station.
options.zh: 申请永久调往出车量较低的站点。

questions.explanationEn: Recurring sleep disturbance and intrusive thoughts after repeated critical incidents are recognized early features of occupational stress injury, and they respond well to early intervention. Peer support normalizes the experience and lowers the threshold to seeking help, while a clinician with experience in trauma provides the evidence-based treatment that peer support alone cannot. A is the mechanism that maintains post-traumatic symptoms: avoidance prevents the memory from being processed and predicts a worse course. B treats one symptom, does nothing for the intrusive thoughts, and further degrades the sleep that is already disturbed. D may have a place within a larger plan, but transferring without treatment leaves the injury untreated and the paramedic still exposed to the next critical call.
questions.explanationZh: 在连续经历危重出车后反复出现睡眠障碍和侵入性回忆，是职业性应激损伤公认的早期表现，而它对早期干预的反应通常很好。同僚支持能让当事人意识到这种反应是常见的，从而降低求助门槛；而具备创伤治疗经验的专业人员，能提供同僚支持无法替代的循证治疗。A 恰恰是维持创伤后症状的机制：回避使记忆无法被加工，预示更差的转归。B 只处理了一个症状，对侵入性回忆毫无作用，还会进一步破坏本已受损的睡眠。D 在整体方案中可能有其位置，但只调岗不治疗，损伤依旧存在，而且下一次危重出车照样会遇到。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with increased work of breathing and a new onset of confusion. Which finding most strongly indicates the need for immediate ventilatory support?
questions.questionZh: 一名82岁、有慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）病史的患者出现呼吸做功增加，并新出现意识模糊。哪一项发现最强烈地提示需要立即给予通气支持？

options.en: A decrease in the patient's level of consciousness.
options.zh: 患者意识水平下降。

options.en: The presence of coarse crackles on auscultation.
options.zh: 听诊闻及粗湿啰音。

options.en: A heart rate of 110 beats per minute.
options.zh: 心率110次/分。

options.en: The use of accessory muscles during inspiration.
options.zh: 吸气时使用辅助呼吸肌。

questions.explanationEn: A falling level of consciousness in a patient who is visibly working to breathe means the work is no longer being sustained: it signals hypercapnic respiratory failure with carbon dioxide narcosis and impending respiratory arrest. BC lists assisting inadequate or failing respirations as indicated for shallow or laboured respirations especially in the presence of decreasing LOC, and the CPAP guideline explicitly excludes patients with a decreased level of consciousness or in imminent or actual respiratory failure, stating that these patients must be ventilated with a bag-valve mask, with a PEEP valve considered. B, C and D are all common findings in an exacerbation and are compatible with a patient who is still compensating; none of them on its own mandates assisted ventilation.
questions.explanationZh: 一个明显在费力呼吸的患者出现意识水平下降，意味着这份呼吸做功已经无法维持：这是高碳酸性呼吸衰竭伴二氧化碳麻醉、即将呼吸骤停的信号。BC 把辅助不足或衰竭的呼吸列为干预指征，特别指出适用于呼吸浅表或费力且伴意识水平下降者；而 CPAP 指南则明确把意识水平下降、以及即将或已经发生呼吸衰竭的患者列为禁忌，规定这类患者必须用球囊面罩通气（可考虑加装 PEEP 阀）。B、C、D 都是急性加重时常见的表现，与仍在代偿的患者并不矛盾，单独任何一项都不构成必须立即辅助通气的理由。

questions.questionEn: During a complex cardiac arrest, the team lead notices that the person performing chest compressions is beginning to fatigue and the rate is slowing. What is the most effective leadership action to maintain high-quality CPR?
questions.questionZh: 在一次复杂的心搏骤停抢救中，团队负责人注意到正在做胸外按压的队员开始疲劳，按压频率变慢。要维持高质量 CPR，最有效的领导行为是什么？

options.en: Instruct the compressor to increase their effort.
options.zh: 指示按压者加大力度。

options.en: Direct a specific team member to take over compressions immediately.
options.zh: 指定某一位具体队员立即接替按压。

options.en: Wait for the compressor to signal they are tired.
options.zh: 等按压者自己示意累了再换人。

options.en: Perform the compressions yourself while continuing to lead.
options.zh: 自己接手按压，同时继续指挥。

questions.explanationEn: BC directs crews to change operators every 2 minutes where possible to maintain maximum efficiency, and to keep any interruption in compressions under 5 seconds. Naming a specific person removes the diffusion of responsibility that follows a general call for help, and the swap is timed to the rhythm analysis so that no additional pause is created. A is ineffective because fatigue is physiological: exhortation does not restore depth, rate or full recoil once the muscles are spent. C is unreliable, since compressors consistently overestimate their own performance and underestimate their fatigue, which is precisely why the change is scheduled rather than requested. D costs the team its leader: the person doing compressions cannot monitor the monitor, the airway, the drugs and the reversible causes at the same time.
questions.explanationZh: BC 要求在条件允许时每 2 分钟更换一次按压者以维持最高效率，并把按压中断控制在 5 秒以内。点名指定具体某个人，可以消除笼统喊一声帮忙时出现的责任分散；把交接安排在心律分析的时间点上，就不会额外制造停顿。A 无效：疲劳是生理性的，肌肉一旦耗竭，再怎么鼓劲也恢复不了按压深度、频率和完全回弹。C 不可靠：按压者普遍高估自己的表现、低估自己的疲劳，这正是要按时间表换人而不是等人开口的原因。D 让团队失去了指挥：正在按压的人无法同时兼顾监护仪、气道、用药和可逆病因。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is reviewing current evidence-based practice guidelines regarding the administration of crystalloid fluids for a patient in compensated shock. Which principle should guide the volume of fluid administered?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正在复习关于代偿期休克（compensated shock）患者使用晶体液的循证实践指南。晶体液的输注量应遵循哪项原则？

options.en: Rapidly infusing fluids until the blood pressure reaches 120/80 mmHg.
options.zh: 快速输液，直到血压达到120/80 mmHg。

options.en: Administering the minimum volume necessary to maintain organ perfusion.
options.zh: 给予维持器官灌注所需的最小量。

options.en: Infusing fluids until the patient's heart rate returns to baseline.
options.zh: 持续输液，直到心率回到基线水平。

options.en: Maintaining a constant high-rate infusion throughout transport.
options.zh: 整个转运过程保持高速率持续输注。

questions.explanationEn: BC's hypovolemia protocol gives the PCP a bolus of 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres, to correct hypoperfusion or hypotension if clinically indicated, reassessing every 500 mL. Fluid is therefore titrated to perfusion rather than to a number on the monitor. Over-resuscitation dilutes clotting factors and haemoglobin, raises pressure enough to displace formed clot, and drops core temperature, all of which worsen outcomes in haemorrhagic shock. A chases a normotensive target that the evidence does not support in uncontrolled bleeding. C uses a poor endpoint, since heart rate is driven by pain, fear and catecholamines as much as by volume, and some patients do not become tachycardic at all. D removes the mandated reassessment and turns a titrated therapy into an uncontrolled one.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的低血容量流程给 PCP 的授权是：在临床有指征时，按 20 ml/kg 给予冲击量、最多 2 升，用于纠正低灌注或低血压，并且每 500 ml 重新评估一次。因此液体是按灌注来滴定的，而不是按监护仪上的某个数字。过度复苏会稀释凝血因子和血红蛋白，把血压顶高到足以冲掉已形成的血凝块，还会降低核心体温——在失血性休克中这三点都会恶化预后。A 追求的正常血压目标，在出血尚未控制的情况下并没有证据支持。C 的终点很差：心率同时受疼痛、恐惧和儿茶酚胺影响，有些患者甚至根本不出现心动过速。D 取消了强制性的重新评估，把一项需要滴定的治疗变成了失控的输注。

questions.questionEn: An elderly patient with mild cognitive impairment is reluctant to undergo a necessary diagnostic test during transport. The patient's adult child, who holds power of attorney, insists that the test be performed. How should the Paramedic proceed to ensure informed consent?
questions.questionZh: 一位有轻度认知障碍（mild cognitive impairment）的老年患者，在转运途中不愿接受一项必要的检查。持有授权书（power of attorney）的成年子女坚持要求做这项检查。Paramedic 应如何处理，才能确保知情同意？

options.en: Perform the test immediately as the power of attorney has been established.
options.zh: 既然授权书已经确立，就立即执行这项检查。

options.en: Defer the test until the patient arrives at the hospital and a physician is present.
options.zh: 把检查推迟到患者抵达医院、有医生在场时再做。

options.en: Explain the benefits and risks of the test to the patient in simple terms to determine their current capacity to consent.
options.zh: 用简单易懂的语言向患者说明这项检查的益处与风险，以判断其当下是否具备同意能力。

options.en: Request the patient's child to sign the consent form on the patient's behalf.
options.zh: 请患者的子女代患者在同意书上签字。

questions.explanationEn: Capacity is decision-specific and time-specific, not a diagnosis. A mild cognitive impairment does not by itself remove the ability to consent to a simple test, and a power of attorney only takes effect for the decisions the patient is actually incapable of making at that moment. The paramedic's obligation is to make the disclosure in a form this patient can understand and then assess whether the patient understands the information and appreciates the consequences of accepting or declining. A treats the power of attorney as a blanket override and risks performing an unconsented procedure on a capable adult. B abandons a decision that is required now and never explores why the patient is reluctant, which is often a fixable concern. D produces a signature that is legally meaningless if the patient is in fact capable.
questions.explanationZh: 决策能力是针对具体决定、具体时点的，而不是一个诊断标签。轻度认知障碍本身并不会剥夺患者对一项简单检查作出同意的能力，而授权书只在患者当下确实无能力作出该决定时才生效。救护员的义务是：用这位患者能理解的方式完成告知，然后评估他是否理解了这些信息、是否能领会接受或拒绝的后果。A 把授权书当成了万能的推翻工具，可能对一位有能力的成年人实施了未经同意的操作。B 回避了此刻就必须作出的决定，也从未去了解患者为什么不愿意——而这往往是可以解决的具体顾虑。D 得到的签字，在患者其实具备能力的情况下没有法律意义。

questions.questionEn: A Paramedic is transporting a patient with chronic complex needs to a facility that is currently experiencing a critical staffing shortage. The facility suggests the Paramedic hold the patient in the ambulance until a bed is ready. Which action best demonstrates patient advocacy in this situation?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正把一位有复杂慢性照护需求的患者送往某机构，而该机构正面临严重的人手短缺。机构建议 Paramedic 让患者先留在救护车上，等床位准备好再交接。哪项做法最能体现患者倡导（patient advocacy）？

options.en: Agree to wait in the ambulance to avoid complicating the facility's staffing issues.
options.zh: 同意在救护车上等待，以免给对方的人手问题添麻烦。

options.en: Advocate for the patient's timely transfer to the facility or an alternative appropriate care setting.
options.zh: 为患者争取及时交接给该机构，或转往另一个合适的照护场所。

options.en: Instruct the patient to contact their family to arrange alternative transportation.
options.zh: 让患者联系家人自行安排其他交通方式。

options.en: Request the facility to provide a written guarantee of the wait time.
options.zh: 要求机构书面保证等待时间。

questions.explanationEn: An offload delay is a clinical problem, not just a logistics inconvenience. A patient held in the back of an ambulance is monitored by one crew with limited equipment, is not receiving the facility's care, cannot use its toilets or beds, and the ambulance itself is removed from the response system for the whole time. Advocacy means pressing for the transfer to happen or, if it genuinely cannot, for an alternative destination that can accept the patient now, and escalating through dispatch or a supervisor if needed. A places the institution's convenience ahead of the patient and normalizes an unsafe practice. C makes a patient with complex needs responsible for a system failure and may leave them with no care at all. D documents the delay without changing anything about it.
questions.explanationZh: 交接延迟（offload delay）是一个临床问题，而不仅仅是后勤上的不便。被滞留在救护车后厢的患者，只有一组人员、有限的设备在监护，得不到该机构的照护，也用不上它的卫生间和床位；与此同时这辆救护车在整个等待期间都脱离了应急服务体系。倡导，意味着推动交接尽快完成；如果确实无法完成，就争取转往另一个此刻能够接收的合适场所，必要时通过调度或主管逐级上报。A 把机构的方便置于患者之上，也把一种不安全的做法常态化。C 让一位有复杂需求的患者为系统性失灵买单，甚至可能导致他完全无人照护。D 只是把延迟记录下来，对延迟本身毫无改变。

questions.questionEn: A 62-year-old male is in cardiac arrest. The team has established IV access and is performing high-quality CPR with an advanced airway in place. The most appropriate next step in the management of this patient's ventilation is to:
questions.questionZh: 一名62岁男性发生心搏骤停。团队已建立静脉通路，正在进行高质量 CPR，且已置入高级气道。此时对该患者通气管理最恰当的下一步是：

options.en: Increase the ventilation rate to 15 breaths per minute.
options.zh: 把通气频率提高到每分钟15次。

options.en: Perform a rescue breath every 2 to 3 seconds.
options.zh: 每2至3秒给予一次人工呼吸。

options.en: Provide one breath every 6 seconds.
options.zh: 每6秒给予一次人工呼吸。

options.en: Synchronize ventilations with chest compressions.
options.zh: 把通气与胸外按压同步进行。

questions.explanationEn: Once an advanced airway is in place, which for a PCP means a supraglottic airway, compressions become continuous and ventilations are delivered asynchronously at one breath every 6 seconds, or 10 per minute. The reason is haemodynamic: every positive pressure breath raises intrathoracic pressure, reduces venous return, and lowers coronary perfusion pressure, which is why BC's CPR principles state plainly that hyperventilation must be avoided. A at 15 per minute and B at every 2 to 3 seconds, which is 20 to 30 per minute and is the paediatric rate with an advanced airway, both hyperventilate an adult. D describes the pre-advanced-airway 30:2 pattern; pausing compressions to synchronize breaths surrenders the main benefit of having placed the airway in the first place.
questions.explanationZh: 一旦置入高级气道（对 PCP 而言就是声门上气道 SGA），胸外按压即转为不间断进行，通气与按压不再同步，按每 6 秒一次（每分钟 10 次）给予。理由是血流动力学：每一次正压通气都会升高胸内压、减少静脉回流、降低冠脉灌注压，这正是 BC 的 CPR 原则中直白写明必须避免过度通气的原因。A 的每分钟 15 次，以及 B 的每 2 至 3 秒一次（相当于每分钟 20 至 30 次，那是儿科在高级气道下的频率），对成人都属于过度通气。D 描述的是尚未置入高级气道时的 30:2 模式；为了同步呼吸而暂停按压，等于放弃了置入高级气道最主要的好处。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old female with a history of congestive heart failure and chronic kidney disease presents with signs of hypovolemic shock due to gastrointestinal bleeding. When administering a crystalloid bolus, the paramedic should prioritize which of the following?
questions.questionZh: 一名78岁女性，既往有充血性心力衰竭（CHF）和慢性肾病（CKD），因消化道出血出现低血容量性休克的表现。在给予晶体液冲击（bolus）时，Paramedic 应优先注意哪一点？

options.en: Rapid infusion of 2 liters to restore blood pressure.
options.zh: 快速输注2升液体以恢复血压。

options.en: Administration of a sympathomimetic to increase heart rate.
options.zh: 给予拟交感神经药物以提升心率。

options.en: Immediate administration of a vasodilator to improve perfusion.
options.zh: 立即给予血管扩张剂以改善灌注。

options.en: Small, frequent boluses with frequent lung auscultation.
options.zh: 小量分次给予液体，并频繁听诊肺部。

questions.explanationEn: BC already builds the safeguard into the protocol: 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres, reassessing every 500 mL. In a patient with heart failure and chronic kidney disease that reassessment is the whole point, because the failing ventricle tolerates a volume load poorly and the kidneys cannot excrete the excess, so the margin between under-resuscitation and pulmonary oedema is narrow. Give the volume the patient needs, in increments, listening to the bases and watching work of breathing and saturation between them. A ignores the mandated reassessment and is the fastest route to iatrogenic pulmonary oedema in this patient. B chases a compensatory response that is already present; the deficit is volume, not rate. C causes cardiovascular collapse in a hypovolaemic patient by dropping preload and afterload further.
questions.explanationZh: BC 已经把安全阀写进了流程：20 ml/kg、最多 2 升，每 500 ml 重新评估一次。对一位同时有心衰和慢性肾病的患者来说，这个重新评估正是关键——衰竭的心室对容量负荷耐受很差，肾脏又排不出多余的液体，补液不足与肺水肿之间的安全区间非常狭窄。正确做法是：分次给予患者确实需要的液体量，每次之间听诊肺底、观察呼吸做功和血氧饱和度。A 无视了强制性的重新评估，对这位患者而言是最快导致医源性肺水肿的方式。B 去追一个本来就已经存在的代偿反应——缺的是容量，不是心率。C 会让本已低血容量的患者进一步降低前负荷和后负荷，导致循环崩溃。

questions.questionEn: During a complex multi-patient incident, a paramedic notices that another team member is preparing to administer a medication that contradicts the established patient care plan. To maintain patient safety and team cohesion, the paramedic should:
questions.questionZh: 在一起复杂的多伤员事件中，一名 Paramedic 注意到另一名队员正准备给药，而该药物与既定的患者照护方案相抵触。为维护患者安全与团队协作，这名 Paramedic 应当：

options.en: Use a closed-loop communication technique to query the action.
options.zh: 使用闭环沟通（closed-loop communication）方式当场确认这一操作。

options.en: Wait until the medication is administered to avoid causing stress.
options.zh: 等药物给完之后再说，以免制造紧张气氛。

options.en: Directly take the medication away from the team member.
options.zh: 直接把药物从该队员手中拿走。

options.en: Ask the team member to leave the scene until the issue is resolved.
options.zh: 要求该队员离开现场，直到问题解决。

questions.explanationEn: The whole value of speaking up is that it happens before the drug reaches the patient. A closed-loop query states the drug, dose, route and patient out loud and asks for confirmation, which takes a few seconds, carries no accusation, and resolves the situation either way: it stops an error, or it corrects the querying paramedic's own misunderstanding of the plan. B allows a suspected error to reach the patient and is the one genuinely unacceptable option. C escalates a clinical check into a physical confrontation, damages the working relationship, and still does not establish what the correct drug is. D removes a resource in the middle of a multi-patient incident and turns a safety check into a disciplinary act; performance concerns belong in a debrief after the call.
questions.explanationZh: 当场发声的全部价值，就在于它发生在药物进入患者体内之前。闭环式的确认是把药名、剂量、途径和对象大声复述出来并请对方确认，只需要几秒钟，不带任何指责，而且无论哪种情况都能解决问题：要么阻止了一次差错，要么纠正了提问者自己对方案的误解。B 让一个已被怀疑的差错落到患者身上，是四个选项中唯一真正不可接受的。C 把一次临床复核升级为肢体冲突，破坏了协作关系，而且仍然没弄清楚正确的药物是什么。D 在多伤员事件中途撤走一名人力资源，把安全复核变成了纪律处分；对表现的关切应留到出车后的复盘中处理。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is managing a patient with a suspected opioid overdose who is being ventilated with a bag-valve mask. The patient's end-tidal CO2 readings are steadily increasing despite consistent ventilation rates. Based on current evidence-informed practice, what is the most appropriate next action?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 正在处置一位疑似阿片类药物过量的患者，并使用球囊面罩（BVM）进行通气。在通气频率保持不变的情况下，患者的呼气末二氧化碳（ETCO2）读数持续上升。依据当前的循证实践，最恰当的下一步是什么？

options.en: Decrease the ventilation rate to allow for CO2 accumulation
options.zh: 降低通气频率，让二氧化碳蓄积

options.en: Increase the ventilation rate to lower the PaCO2
options.zh: 提高通气频率，以降低动脉血二氧化碳分压（PaCO2）

options.en: Immediately switch to a higher concentration of oxygen
options.zh: 立即改用更高浓度的氧气

options.en: Cease ventilations to assess the patient's own respiratory drive
options.zh: 停止通气，以观察患者自身的呼吸驱动

questions.explanationEn: In opioid toxicity the primary derangement is hypoventilation: a depressed rate and small tidal volumes producing carbon dioxide retention. A steadily climbing end-tidal CO2 at an unchanged ventilation rate means minute ventilation is not keeping up, so the corrective action is to increase the rate, while also confirming that each breath produces visible chest rise and that the mask seal is adequate. BC's suspected narcotic overdose guideline requires that ventilations be supported as required, with two-person BVM technique considered and saturation maintained at or above 94 percent. A is the opposite of what is needed and deepens the respiratory acidosis. C corrects hypoxia but does nothing about carbon dioxide, which is cleared only by ventilation. D withdraws the treatment keeping the patient alive in order to gather information that does not change the immediate need for ventilation.
questions.explanationZh: 阿片类中毒的核心紊乱是通气不足：呼吸频率被抑制、潮气量偏小，导致二氧化碳潴留。在通气频率不变的情况下 ETCO2 持续上升，说明分钟通气量跟不上，纠正措施就是提高通气频率，同时确认每次通气都能看到胸廓起伏、面罩密封良好。BC 的疑似麻醉品过量指南要求按需支持通气，可考虑双人 BVM 技术，并把血氧饱和度维持在 94% 及以上。A 与所需处置完全相反，只会加重呼吸性酸中毒。C 能纠正低氧，但对二氧化碳毫无作用——二氧化碳只能靠通气排出。D 为了获取一项并不会改变当下通气需求的信息，却撤掉了正在维持患者生命的治疗。

questions.questionEn: While monitoring an adult patient, the paramedic observes a sinus rhythm where the PR interval is consistently 0.24 seconds and the QRS complex is narrow. Which interpretation is most accurate?
questions.questionZh: 在监护一名成年患者时，Paramedic 观察到窦性节律，PR 间期恒定为 0.24 秒，QRS 波群窄。以下哪项判读最准确？

options.en: First-degree AV block.
options.zh: 一度房室传导阻滞（first-degree AV block）。

options.en: Second-degree AV block type I.
options.zh: 二度I型房室传导阻滞（文氏现象）。

options.en: Second-degree AV block type II.
options.zh: 二度II型房室传导阻滞。

options.en: Third-degree AV block.
options.zh: 三度（完全性）房室传导阻滞。

questions.explanationEn: A PR interval that is constant and longer than 0.20 seconds, with every P wave followed by a QRS, is by definition first-degree AV block: conduction through the AV node is delayed but nothing is dropped. B, Wenckebach, requires progressive lengthening of the PR interval until a QRS is dropped and the cycle repeats. C requires dropped QRS complexes with an otherwise constant PR interval. D requires atrioventricular dissociation, with P waves and QRS complexes marching independently and usually a slow escape rhythm. Recognizing the rhythm matters clinically because isolated first-degree block in an asymptomatic patient needs no treatment; the value lies in not over-treating it and in flagging it as a baseline finding for the receiving team.
questions.explanationZh: PR 间期恒定且超过 0.20 秒，同时每一个 P 波后面都跟着一个 QRS 波，按定义就是一度房室传导阻滞：房室结传导变慢，但没有任何一次搏动被漏掉。B（文氏现象）要求 PR 间期逐搏延长，直到漏掉一个 QRS，然后周而复始。C 要求出现漏搏，而漏搏之外的 PR 间期保持恒定。D 要求房室分离，P 波与 QRS 波各自独立地按自己的节律出现，通常伴有缓慢的逸搏心律。正确识别这一节律的临床意义在于：无症状患者的单纯一度阻滞不需要处理，价值在于不去过度治疗它，同时把它作为基线所见告知接收团队。

questions.questionEn: During the assessment of an unconscious adult patient, the paramedic notes that the patient is breathing 6 times per minute with shallow chest rise. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate intervention?
questions.questionZh: 在评估一名无意识的成年患者时，Paramedic 发现患者呼吸频率为每分钟6次，胸廓起伏浅。最恰当的即时处置是哪一项？

options.en: Position the patient in the recovery position.
options.zh: 把患者置于复原卧位。

options.en: Administer a sympathomimetic bronchodilator.
options.zh: 给予拟交感支气管扩张剂。

options.en: Perform a rapid primary survey of the airway.
options.zh: 对气道做一次快速初步检查。

options.en: Initiate assisted ventilation with a bag-valve mask.
options.zh: 使用球囊面罩开始辅助通气。

questions.explanationEn: Six breaths per minute with shallow chest rise is grossly inadequate minute ventilation, and in an unconscious patient it will produce hypoxia and progressive carbon dioxide retention within minutes. BC lists assisting inadequate or failing respirations as indicated for abnormally fast or slow respirations and for shallow or laboured respirations, especially with a decreasing level of consciousness; this patient meets both criteria. A leaves the hypoventilation untreated and only addresses airway protection. B treats bronchospasm, which is not the problem described and would not improve a depressed respiratory drive. C is a necessary activity rather than an intervention, and the assessment finding that mandates ventilation is already in the stem; delaying assisted ventilation in order to reassess is precisely the error being tested.
questions.explanationZh: 每分钟 6 次、胸廓起伏浅，意味着分钟通气量严重不足；在无意识患者身上，几分钟内就会造成低氧和进行性的二氧化碳潴留。BC 把辅助不足或衰竭的呼吸列为干预指征，适用于呼吸过快或过慢，以及呼吸浅表或费力（尤其伴意识水平下降）者——本例两条都满足。A 只解决了气道保护，通气不足依旧没有处理。B 针对的是支气管痉挛，既不是本题的问题，也无法改善被抑制的呼吸驱动。C 是必须做的动作而非干预措施，而且题干中已经给出了要求立即通气的评估发现；为了再评估而推迟辅助通气，正是本题要考的错误。

questions.questionEn: While managing a pediatric patient in respiratory distress, a paramedic determines that the patient requires assisted ventilation. Which action is most appropriate to ensure effective ventilation while minimizing the risk of gastric inflation?
questions.questionZh: 在处置一名呼吸窘迫的儿科患者时，Paramedic 判断该患儿需要辅助通气。哪项做法最能保证有效通气，同时把胃胀气（gastric inflation）的风险降到最低？

options.en: Utilize a neutral head position and deliver small, controlled breaths.
options.zh: 保持头部中立位，并给予小量、可控的通气。

options.en: Place the patient in a Trendelenburg position to improve blood flow.
options.zh: 把患儿置于头低脚高位以改善血流。

options.en: Hyperventilate the patient to ensure maximum oxygen saturation.
options.zh: 对患儿进行过度通气，以求达到最高的血氧饱和度。

options.en: Insert an oropharyngeal airway regardless of the gag reflex.
options.zh: 无论有无咽反射都置入口咽通气道。

questions.explanationEn: Gastric inflation occurs when airway pressure exceeds the pressure of the lower oesophageal sphincter, which happens when breaths are delivered too fast, too forcefully, or through a partly obstructed airway. In small children the airway is most patent in a neutral position rather than an extended one, which is why BC recommends a pad under the shoulders in infants to offset the large occiput and achieve neutral alignment. Each breath should be just enough to produce visible chest rise, delivered over about a second. A distended stomach splints the diaphragm, reduces tidal volume and sharply raises the risk of regurgitation and aspiration. B has no effect on ventilation and pushes abdominal contents against the diaphragm. C is the direct cause of gastric inflation and also reduces venous return. D risks laryngospasm and vomiting in a child with an intact gag reflex.
questions.explanationZh: 胃胀气发生在气道压力超过食管下段括约肌压力的时候，而这通常源于送气过快、过猛，或气道部分梗阻。幼儿的气道在中立位下最通畅，而不是在过度后仰位——这也是 BC 建议给婴儿肩下垫一块衬垫、抵消其较大枕部以取得中立位的原因。每一次通气量只要刚好能看到胸廓起伏即可，送气时间约一秒。胃部膨胀会顶住膈肌、减少潮气量，并大幅增加反流误吸的风险。B 对通气毫无帮助，还把腹腔内容物推向膈肌。C 正是造成胃胀气的直接原因，同时还减少静脉回流。D 在咽反射完好的儿童身上置入口咽通气道，可能诱发喉痉挛和呕吐。

questions.questionEn: During the resuscitation of an adult patient in cardiac arrest, the paramedic observes that the chest is not rising during ventilations. After repositioning the head, the chest still does not rise. What is the most appropriate next action?
questions.questionZh: 在抢救一名成人心搏骤停患者时，Paramedic 发现通气时胸廓没有起伏。重新调整头部位置后，胸廓仍然不起伏。最恰当的下一步是什么？

options.en: Attempt to insert a supraglottic airway device.
options.zh: 尝试置入声门上气道装置（supraglottic airway, SGA）。

options.en: Increase the pressure of the ventilations.
options.zh: 加大通气时的压力。

options.en: Perform a blind finger sweep of the oropharynx.
options.zh: 对口咽部做盲目手指清扫。

options.en: Switch to a different bag-valve mask.
options.zh: 换一个球囊面罩装置。

questions.explanationEn: Failure to ventilate after repositioning means the basic manoeuvre is not producing a patent, sealed airway. BC allows PCPs to insert a supraglottic airway once high-quality cardiac arrest management is under way, and an SGA solves both of the common causes at once: it bypasses soft-tissue obstruction at the level of the pharynx and it eliminates the mask seal, which is the single most frequent reason bag-valve-mask ventilation fails during an arrest. B forces gas preferentially into the stomach rather than the lungs, producing gastric inflation, regurgitation and aspiration. C is contraindicated, because a blind sweep can drive a foreign body deeper and injure the airway; obstructions are removed under direct vision or with suction. D assumes equipment failure, which is far less likely than a seal or anatomical problem and wastes time in a patient receiving no oxygen at all.
questions.explanationZh: 重新摆位后仍无法通气，说明基础手法没能形成一个既通畅又密封的气道。BC 允许 PCP 在高质量心搏骤停管理已经展开后置入声门上气道，而 SGA 同时解决了两个常见原因：它绕过咽部水平的软组织梗阻，也彻底消除了面罩密封问题——而后者正是心搏骤停中 BVM 通气失败最常见的单一原因。B 会把气体优先压进胃里而不是肺里，造成胃胀气、反流和误吸。C 属于禁忌：盲目手指清扫可能把异物推得更深并损伤气道；清除梗阻应在直视下或使用吸引器完成。D 预设了设备故障，而这种可能性远低于密封或解剖学问题，却在一个完全没有获得氧合的患者身上白白浪费时间。

questions.questionEn: During a mass casualty incident, a Primary Care Paramedic is conducting triage. A patient is found lying supine, unresponsive, with no spontaneous respirations. After manually opening the airway, the patient begins breathing normally. What is the most appropriate triage category for this patient?
questions.questionZh: 在一起大规模伤亡事件（MCI）中，一名 PCP 正在执行检伤分类。一名患者仰卧、无反应、没有自主呼吸。用手法打开气道后，患者开始正常呼吸。该患者最恰当的分类等级是什么？

options.en: Delayed (Yellow)
options.zh: 延迟处理（黄标）

options.en: Immediate (Red)
options.zh: 立即处理（红标）

options.en: Minor (Green)
options.zh: 轻伤（绿标）

options.en: Deceased (Black)
options.zh: 死亡（黑标）

questions.explanationEn: Primary triage sorts on respirations, perfusion and mental status. A patient who is apnoeic but who breathes as soon as the airway is manually opened is categorized Immediate: the airway does not stay open on its own, the patient is entirely dependent on a positional intervention, and unresponsiveness alone already places them in the highest category. D is the trap in this item, because apnoea sorts to Deceased only if the patient still does not breathe after a single airway-opening manoeuvre, which is the one intervention permitted during primary triage. A and C both describe patients who are breathing spontaneously with adequate perfusion and who can follow commands, and Green additionally implies a patient able to walk to the treatment area, none of which applies here.
questions.explanationZh: 初级检伤分类依据呼吸、灌注和意识状态三项来分级。一名本来没有呼吸、但在手法开放气道后立即恢复呼吸的患者，应归为立即处理（红标）：气道无法自行保持通畅，患者完全依赖体位性干预，而单是无反应这一点就已经把他放进最高优先级。D 是本题的陷阱：只有在完成一次开放气道手法（这也是初级分类阶段唯一允许的干预）之后仍然没有呼吸，才归为死亡（黑标）。A 与 C 描述的都是自主呼吸、灌注尚可、能听从指令的患者，绿标更意味着患者能自行走到治疗区——本例均不符合。

questions.questionEn: When establishing intravenous access in an adult patient, which anatomical landmark is most reliable for locating the cephalic vein in the forearm?
questions.questionZh: 在为成年患者建立静脉通路时，定位前臂头静脉（cephalic vein）最可靠的解剖标志是哪一个？

options.en: The ulnar artery pulse point.
options.zh: 尺动脉搏动点。

options.en: The radial side of the forearm.
options.zh: 前臂的桡侧（拇指侧）。

options.en: The midline of the antecubital fossa.
options.zh: 肘窝的正中线。

options.en: The medial side of the wrist.
options.zh: 腕部的尺侧（内侧）。

questions.explanationEn: The cephalic vein runs up the radial, or lateral thumb, side of the forearm from the anatomical snuffbox toward the shoulder, which makes it a reliable and relatively straight target that is easy to stabilize. A points to the opposite, ulnar side of the forearm and is an arterial landmark rather than a venous one. C describes where the median cubital vein crosses the antecubital fossa; that vein is a different and more proximal site, and a catheter placed across a joint kinks and positionally occludes. D is where the basilic vein lies, on the ulnar side of the wrist. Site selection has practical consequences: BC's stroke guideline, for example, directs the PCP to select a site above the level of the wrist using an 18 gauge catheter, preferably on the right side.
questions.explanationZh: 头静脉沿前臂的桡侧（即拇指侧、外侧）从解剖学鼻烟窝一路上行至肩部，走行相对笔直、容易固定，是可靠的穿刺目标。A 指向的是前臂的对侧（尺侧），而且它是动脉标志而非静脉标志。C 描述的是肘正中静脉横过肘窝的位置——那是另一个更靠近心端的穿刺点，而且导管跨关节留置容易打折，并随体位改变而阻塞。D 是贵要静脉（basilic vein）的位置，在腕部尺侧。穿刺点的选择有实际影响：例如 BC 的卒中处置指南就要求 PCP 在腕关节水平以上选点、使用 18 G 导管，并优先选择右侧。

questions.questionEn: A Primary Care Paramedic is treating an adult patient in hypovolemic shock. After initiating a crystalloid bolus, the patient's blood pressure remains unchanged, but their heart rate decreases and their mental status improves. Which action is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 PCP 正在处置一位低血容量性休克的成年患者。给予晶体液冲击后，患者血压没有变化，但心率下降、意识状态改善。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Increase the rate of the crystalloid infusion.
options.zh: 加快晶体液的输注速度。

options.en: Continue monitoring the patient's response.
options.zh: 继续监测患者的反应。

options.en: Immediately notify the physician to request a vasopressor.
options.zh: 立即联系医生，申请使用升压药。

options.en: Discontinue the crystalloid bolus.
options.zh: 停止晶体液冲击。

questions.explanationEn: Perfusion, not blood pressure, is the endpoint of fluid resuscitation. A falling heart rate together with improving mentation are the earliest and most reliable signs that organ perfusion is recovering, because both reflect reduced catecholamine drive and better cerebral flow. Blood pressure is a late and insensitive marker, maintained by compensation until it fails, so it commonly lags well behind the clinical improvement. BC requires reassessment every 500 mL within the 20 mL/kg bolus to a maximum of 2 litres, and that reassessment is exactly what has just happened, so the plan continues. A escalates therapy in a patient who is already responding, risking dilution, clot disruption and cooling. C is premature and outside PCP scope. D withdraws a therapy that is demonstrably working.
questions.explanationZh: 液体复苏的终点是灌注，而不是血压。心率下降与意识状态改善，是器官灌注正在恢复的最早、也最可靠的征象，因为二者都反映了儿茶酚胺驱动减弱和脑血流改善。血压则是迟钝而滞后的指标——在代偿失败之前它一直被维持住，因此常常明显落后于临床改善。BC 要求在 20 ml/kg（最多 2 升）的冲击量中每 500 ml 重新评估一次，而刚刚发生的正是这次重新评估，因此按原方案继续即可。A 在患者已经有反应的情况下继续加码，带来稀释、冲掉血凝块和降温的风险。C 既为时过早，升压药也不在 PCP 的授权范围内。D 停掉了一个明显正在起效的治疗。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old patient in cardiac arrest has a valid Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order, but the family is demanding full resuscitative efforts. The paramedic team is experiencing conflict regarding the ethical obligations of care. Which action best demonstrates professional accountability in this situation?
questions.questionZh: 一名78岁患者发生心搏骤停，持有有效的「不予复苏」（DNR）医嘱，但家属要求进行全面复苏。救护团队内部对照护的伦理义务产生了分歧。哪项做法最能体现专业问责（professional accountability）？

options.en: Defer the decision entirely to the family members present.
options.zh: 把决定完全交给在场的家属。

options.en: Consult the DNR order and the patient's advance directives to guide care.
options.zh: 查验 DNR 医嘱与患者的预先指示，并据此指导处置。

options.en: Initiate full resuscitation and allow the physician to decide later.
options.zh: 先进行全面复苏，把决定留给之后的医生。

options.en: Follow the most recent provincial legislation regarding DNR orders.
options.zh: 按最新的省级立法关于 DNR 的规定处理。

questions.explanationEn: BC lists a verifiable Do Not Resuscitate or No CPR order as a contraindication to CPR, and directs that resuscitation efforts are also stopped when a valid order is produced. The patient's own previously expressed, capable wish governs, so accountability means verifying that the order is valid and applies to this patient, following it, and then supporting the family through what is often the hardest moment of their lives, including explaining what the order means and what care is still being given. A substitutes the family's wishes for the patient's; distress is real but relatives cannot override a valid directive. C is a decision by default, imposing an unconsented and invasive intervention on a patient who has explicitly declined it. D sounds authoritative but is not actionable at the bedside and is how the option set disguises inaction.
questions.explanationZh: BC 把可核实的「不予复苏」（DNR）或「不做 CPR」医嘱列为 CPR 的禁忌，并规定在出示有效医嘱时应停止复苏。起支配作用的是患者本人此前在有能力时表达的意愿，因此所谓专业问责，就是核实这份医嘱有效且适用于本患者、遵照执行，然后在很可能是家属一生中最难熬的时刻陪伴和支持他们，包括解释这份医嘱意味着什么、目前仍在提供哪些照护。A 用家属的意愿取代了患者的意愿；家属的痛苦是真实的，但他们不能推翻一份有效的预先指示。C 是一种默认式的决定：对一位已明确拒绝的患者强加了未经同意的侵入性处置。D 听起来很有权威，却在床边无法执行，是这组选项用来伪装成不作为的说法。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is transporting an elderly patient who asks directly if they are going to die based on their current clinical condition. Which response best demonstrates professional communication and conflict management in this challenging conversation?
questions.questionZh: 一名 Paramedic 在转运一位老年患者时，患者直接问：以我现在的状况，我是不是要死了？哪种回应最能体现专业沟通与困难对话的处理能力？

options.en: Tell the patient that only a doctor can provide a prognosis.
options.zh: 告诉患者只有医生才能给出预后判断。

options.en: Provide an honest, empathetic response while encouraging discussion with the medical team.
options.zh: 给予诚实且有同理心的回应，同时鼓励患者与医疗团队进一步讨论。

options.en: Avoid the question to prevent the patient from becoming more distressed.
options.zh: 回避这个问题，以免患者更加不安。

options.en: Reassure the patient that everything will be fine regardless of the situation.
options.zh: 不论实际情况如何，都安慰患者说一切都会好起来。

questions.explanationEn: Answering honestly does not mean delivering a prognosis you are not in a position to give. It means not lying, acknowledging the fear behind the question, saying what you can actually see and what you are doing about it, and connecting the patient to the team who can answer the larger question. That combination respects the patient's right to information and keeps the therapeutic relationship intact at the moment it matters most. A is technically true but functions as a brush-off and leaves a frightened person alone with the question. C abandons the patient precisely when presence is the intervention, and silence is usually interpreted as the worst possible answer. D is false reassurance: it collapses the moment reality contradicts it, and it destroys the credibility of everything else the paramedic has said.
questions.explanationZh: 诚实回答并不等于给出一个你没有资格给出的预后判断。它意味着：不撒谎、承认问题背后的恐惧、说出你此刻确实看到的情况和正在采取的措施，并把患者与能够回答这个更大问题的团队连接起来。这样的组合既尊重了患者的知情权，也在最要紧的时刻保住了治疗性关系。A 在字面上没错，但实际效果是打发人，让一个害怕的人独自面对这个问题。C 恰恰在陪伴本身就是治疗的时刻抛下了患者，而沉默通常会被理解成最坏的答案。D 是虚假的安慰：一旦现实与之矛盾就立刻崩塌，同时也毁掉了救护员此前所说一切话的可信度。
